title: Lost Cabin data center part of $66 billion plan
source_used: The Ranger (Riverton) as carried by WyomingNews.com
key_facts: At a Fremont County commissioners meeting on Tuesday (6 Oct 2026), commissioners said the Lost Cabin data centre now being built is phase one of a $66 billion project.
Commission Chair Larry Allen said the current building costs $16 million, the electronics another $22 million, and the planned project will have $66 billion invested.
Planning Director Steve Baumann said the plans include natural gas reciprocating generators of 500 MW capacity, none of which would feed the grid.
Fremont County has no zoning regulations and little control; the larger project would likely need approval from Wyoming's Industrial Siting Council.
The company behind it is registered as ETC DC OpCo; Baumann said he deals with Aethel Energy; Aethel Energy and Electio Technologies are both backed by General Catalyst.
The current small facility has state fire marshal approval and an air-quality approval for backup generators and expects power from High Plains by late October or early November.
The closest residents are about a mile away, according to Baumann.
quote_evidence: "The one they are planning now, they will have $66 billion invested."
As those concerns have come to Fremont County, it's become clear that the county's lack of zoning regulations means that the county has little control over whether such projects will go forward.
why_it_matters_hint: A small data centre is the first phase of a vastly larger, self-powered project in a county without zoning.
event_date: Tue 6 Oct 2026 (date inferred from 'Tuesday' in an article published 9 Oct)
notes: The $66 billion figure was said by a commissioner and is not confirmed by the company in the article. Outlet inferred: the text refers to 'The Ranger' as its own earlier interview.
